questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Design Philosophies (Working Stress Method vs Limit State Method)
questions.text: Compare Working Stress Method (WSM) vs Ultimate Load Method (ULM) vs Limit State Method (LSM) (IS 456:2000). Explain Limit State of Collapse vs Limit State of Serviceability (Deflection and Cracking). State partial safety factors for materials ($\gamma_c = 1.5, \gamma_s = 1.15$) and load combinations.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Limit State Design of Beams in Flexure (Singly and Doubly Reinforced)
questions.text: Explain Stress-Strain block diagram for Singly Reinforced Rectangular beam under Limit State Method. Derive formula for depth of neutral axis ($x_u = \frac{0.87 f_y A_{st}}{0.36 f_{ck} b}$) and limiting moment of resistance ($M_{u,lim} = 0.138 f_{ck} b d^2$ for Fe415). Differentiate under-reinforced, balanced, and over-reinforced sections.

questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Limit State Design of Beams in Flexure (Singly and Doubly Reinforced)
questions.text: Design a Doubly Reinforced Rectangular Beam of size $250 \text{ mm} \times 500 \text{ mm}$ effective depth to resist an ultimate factored bending moment $M_u = 220 \text{ kNm}$. Use M20 grade concrete and Fe415 steel with effective cover $d' = 50 \text{ mm}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Limit State Design of Beams for Shear, Torsion, and Bond/Anchorage
questions.text: Explain Shear failure mechanisms in RCC beams (Diagonal Tension, Diagonal Compression). Calculate nominal shear stress $\tau_v = \frac{V_u}{b d}$ and design vertical 2-legged shear stirrups ($A_{sv}$) for a factored shear force $V_u = 120 \text{ kN}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Limit State Design of Beams for Shear, Torsion, and Bond/Anchorage
questions.text: Define Development Length ($L_d = \frac{\phi \sigma_s}{4 \tau_{bd}}$) of reinforcing bars. Explain mechanism of bond failure (Flexural bond vs Anchorage bond) and curtailment of tension reinforcement.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Limit State Design of Slabs (One-Way and Two-Way Slabs)
questions.text: Differentiate between One-Way Slab ($l_y / l_x > 2$) and Two-Way Slab ($l_y / l_x \le 2$). Design a Two-Way Simply Supported RCC Slab of size $4 \text{ m} \times 5 \text{ m}$ supporting a live load of $4 \text{ kN/m}^2$ and floor finish $1 \text{ kN/m}^2$ using IS 456:2000 moment coefficients. Apply check for shear and deflection.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Limit State Design of Columns (Short Axially Loaded and Uniaxial/Biaxial Bending)
questions.text: Differentiate between Short Column vs Slender (Long) Column. Explain minimum eccentricity requirement ($e_{min} = \frac{L}{500} + \frac{D}{30} \ge 20 \text{ mm}$). Design a Short Square RCC Column to support an axial factored load $P_u = 1500 \text{ kN}$ using M20 concrete and Fe415 steel with lateral ties.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Design of Footings (Isolated Pad and Sloped Footing) and Retaining Walls
questions.text: Design an Isolated Square Pad Footing for a square column $400 \text{ mm} \times 400 \text{ mm}$ transmitting an axial load $P = 1000 \text{ kN}$. Safe bearing capacity of soil $SBC = 180 \text{ kN/m}^2$. Perform checks for: (a) One-way shear, (b) Two-way (Punching) shear, and (c) Development length.
